record.prompt: Please run scripts/cost.sh on data/orders-2026-10.tsv and tell me the total shipping cost for October. Don't edit the script or data/zone-rates.tsv.

base_changes.keywords: cost.sh zone-rates.tsv CRLF no rate for zone
base_changes.content: scripts/cost.sh fails with 'no rate for zone "north"' because data/zone-rates.tsv has CRLF line endings (zone keys end in \r). Workaround without editing files: pass a CR-stripped copy as the second argument, e.g. tr -d '\r' < data/zone-rates.tsv > /tmp/rates.tsv; scripts/cost.sh ORDERS /tmp/rates.tsv.

record.final_answer:
**October's total shipping cost is 58.01**, across 6 orders.

| Order | Zone | Cost |
|---|---|---|
| A-1001 | north | 6.94 |
| A-1002 | south | 6.28 |
| A-1003 | island | 15.25 |
| A-1004 | north | 15.10 |
| A-1005 | south | 9.03 |
| A-1006 | north | 5.41 |

The first run failed with `no rate for zone "north"`. The cause is that `data/zone-rates.tsv` uses Windows (CRLF) line endings, so the script reads each zone name with a hidden `\r` on the end and can't match it to the orders. The orders file is fine.

To get the numbers without editing anything, I made a temporary copy of the rates file with the `\r` removed and gave it to `cost.sh` as its optional second argument (rates file). The script and both data files are unchanged. I checked one row by hand: north is 4.90 + 0.85 × 2.4 = 6.94, which matches.

If you want the script to work with no workaround, convert `zone-rates.tsv` to Unix line endings, or have the script strip `\r` when it reads the file. I didn't make either change because you asked me not to. I also saved this problem and the workaround to memory so later sessions will know about it.
